chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: How Lena Horne joined the band at the Casino Theater
summary: With his singers hoarse, Barnet asked the Apollo's Clarence Robinson for help and Lena Horne was fetched from a movie; she stayed about nine months.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: How -- tell me about Lena Horne working with the band.
Well, Lena came to us under a distressed circumstances on our part, and strangely enough through the Apollo. We were playing a two day theater up in the Bronx

called the Casino Theater, and I had a -- I had Ford Leary and Bob Carroll and I had a girl singer, too. I can't remember what her name was. Anyway, they all came down with laryngitis. Not one of them could make a sound. And this was one of these theaters where the band was the whole show. We had to play, put on, you know, an hour, hour and ten minute show, and if you've got no vocalists there again we get back to what I was talking about earlier, the static idea of watching a band play without something else happening. You know, when people are sitting there they want to see something. So in a panic I said, "My goodness, we're going to have to get somebody up here that can do something." So I called Clarence Robinson at the Apollo, who was like a producer and the dance director, and I said, "Clarence, is there anybody around there that can get up here so they can do something?" And I wasn't thinking as much of a singer as maybe some kind of an act or something. And he says, "Well, I don't know. A girl just left here," and he said, "She went down to the theater to go to the movies. I'll see if I can find her." Well, Clarence went down the street and went into the movies and ran up and down the aisle and found Lena sitting in there, and he said, "Get your gown and get up to the Casino Theater right away." So Lena came in. I'd never met her before. I didn't know who she was or anything, but naturally she's a very beautiful lady. So we had a talkover rehearsal down underneath the

stage, and she went on, and this was -- believe it or not this was an Irish neighborhood in the Bronx, and they are inclined to be very chintzy about -- like the manager came back and he said, "I don't know what's going to happen here." I said, "Never mind." And she went on and broke it up. And then of course I asked her to stay and she did, and she was with us for, oh, I think about nine months after that.

Did you read in her book where she said that she was all packed and ready to go back home to wherever it was that she'd been living with her husband that she was no longer really with, but back home to give up show business? She had her bags all packed --
-- in the YMCA and she for some reason didn't leave that minute, and instead decided to go see a movie because she was so depressed, and that was when Clarence Robinson came for her.
